title: Perf-canary: add synthetic overload scenarios + CI gating to catch overload regressions
creator: Tomáš Novák
project: Reliability Program — Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding
description:
## Summary
Add synthetic overload scenarios to perf-canary and wire them into CI gating so we can catch regressions that re-introduce tail-latency collapse, queue runaway, or ambiguous 5xx/timeouts under overload.

This is specifically meant to validate the Hosted circuit breaker + load shedding work end-to-end (gateway → routing → runtime) and prevent future changes from accidentally:
- removing early shed behavior,
- increasing recovery time after a spike,
- causing breaker flapping,
- reintroducing retry-storm-friendly error mixes.

## Why
We have multiple incidents where “normal” perf tests looked fine, but under spike conditions p99 exploded and the system took minutes to recover. We need a repeatable, automated overload harness that runs frequently enough to stop regressions before canary/prod.

## Scope
### New perf-canary scenarios
1) **Step-function spike (burst)**
- Warmup 2–3 min at baseline RPS
- Instant jump to N× baseline for 60–180s
- Recovery window 5–10 min back at baseline

2) **Long-prompt spike (prefill pressure)**
- Mixture distribution with periodic large context requests (e.g., 8k–16k tokens)
- Validates prefill shed behavior + queue bounding

3) **Mixed streaming/non-streaming**
- Ensure we preferentially shed before stream starts; detect increased mid-stream disconnect rates

4) **Multi-tenant mix (fairness smoke)**
- Two synthetic tenants (high-volume + low-volume)
- Verify low-volume tenant doesn’t get starved disproportionately when shedding is active (coarse smoke test; not a full fairness proof)

### Gating and pass/fail rules
We will gate on *regression* vs a pinned baseline plus hard ceilings.

**Primary signals** (per scenario):
- p95/p99 end-to-end latency (separate streaming time-to-first-token where applicable)
- error mix (429/503 “overload-protected” vs internal 5xx)
- recovery time (time for p99 to return within X% of baseline after spike ends)
- shed rate and shed reasons (if reason codes present)

**Hard ceilings (initial defaults; tuned post-canary):**
- Internal 5xx under overload: < 0.5% of requests (excluding explicit overload-protected errors)
- p99 latency during spike: must not exceed baseline_p99 * 4 (route/model-specific overrides allowed)
- Recovery: p99 must return to within 1.5× baseline within 5 minutes after the spike ends
- Breaker flapping proxy (if breaker-transition metric available): < 3 transitions / 10 min per (model, region, tier)

### CI integration plan
- **PR gating (fast path):** run shortened versions of scenarios (1–3 min spike, smaller duration) to keep runtime reasonable.
- **Nightly (full):** longer duration to reduce flake and measure recovery characteristics.
- Store artifacts:
  - scenario config
  - summary JSON with metrics
  - links to Grafana snapshot (if available in the environment)

## Non-goals
- Replace existing load tests or benchmark suites.
- Perfect modeling of real customer traffic distributions.
- Building a full fairness certification suite (this is a smoke test only).

## Acceptance criteria
- New scenarios exist in perf-canary with deterministic seeds and documented configs.
- CI job runs in PRs (fast path) and fails on defined regressions.
- Nightly job runs full scenarios and publishes artifacts.
- At least one successful run against canary environment with overload-protection flags enabled, producing a shareable report.

## Implementation notes
- Prefer stable signals over single-point thresholds: compare medians over multiple short runs in PR gating.
- Keep label cardinality bounded in any new metrics consumed by the harness; prefer aggregations by (region, model, tier) only.

## Links
- GitHub: perf-canary PR (planned) — `sources/github/perf-canary/pr-97.json`
- Umbrella initiative: ENG-4821
- Related telemetry work: ENG-4829
